questions.cardText:
[Physiology and Anatomy] Which of the following functions is primarily controlled by the brain stem?
A. Voluntary movements
B. Breathing
C. Cognition
Answer: B. In 1945, a chicken named Mike lived for 18 months after his head was cut off. Mike survived because a significant part of his brain stem, or its equivalence that controls basic life functions, remained intact.
questions.de: Welcher Teil des Gehirns, der Atmung und Herzschlag regelt, blieb beim kopflosen Huhn Mike weitgehend erhalten und ließ es nach seiner Enthauptung noch 18 Monate leben?
questions.en: Which part of the brain, which regulates breathing and heart rate, stayed largely intact in Mike the Headless Chicken and let him live for 18 months after his beheading?

timeline.labelEn: Farmer Lloyd Olsen beheads Mike the chicken in Fruita, Colorado; Mike survives for 18 months
timeline.labelDe: Farmer Lloyd Olsen köpft in Fruita, Colorado, das Huhn Mike, das danach noch 18 Monate lebt

questions.notes: Reworked to ask the brain part (the card's options-free form “what does the brain stem control?” has several answers: breathing, heart rate). Brainstem article: regulates heart and respiratory function.

questions.cardText:
[Zoology] What characteristic does a platypus exhibit under ultraviolet light?
A. Its fur changes color continuously
B. It glows
C. The fur becomes semi-transparent
Answer: B. According to recent findings, the fur of a platypus glows with a blue-green fluorescence under ultraviolet light.
questions.de: In welcher Farbe leuchtet das Fell eines Schnabeltiers unter ultraviolettem Licht?
questions.en: What colour does the fur of a platypus glow under ultraviolet light?

timeline.labelEn: Paula Spaeth Anich and colleagues report biofluorescence in the platypus
timeline.labelDe: Paula Spaeth Anich und Kollegen berichten über Biofluoreszenz beim Schnabeltier

questions.notes: Wikipedia: glows cyan and green under UV light (Anich et al., Mammalia, 2020).
